title: Black hole radial geometry from a quantum spin chain
abstract: We show that the radial differential equation for a scalar field in an anti-de Sitter black brane background can be encoded in an exactly solvable semi-infinite spin chain independent of dimensionality. The radial coordinate emerges as lattice quasimomentum. Spin coherence encodes the geometry, while the spectrum and response recover gravitational observables and yield exact screening-mass sum rules. We implement the finite chain on a superconducting processor. At finite filling and low energies, the model yields a conformal field theory in a coordinate proportional to proper radial distance.

bite.hook: Encoding a black hole's radial geometry into an exactly solvable quantum spin chain.
tldr: Showed that the radial differential equation for a scalar field in a black brane background can be encoded in a spin chain.
Implemented the finite chain on a superconducting processor.
Recovered gravitational observables, exact screening-mass sum rules, and a conformal field theory at low energies.
bite.whyItMatters: Connecting gravitational physics like black holes to controllable quantum systems like spin chains opens up new ways to simulate complex cosmic phenomena using laboratory hardware.
bite.eli5: Think of translating the complex geometry of a black hole into a simple row of microscopic magnets interacting with each other. By studying how the magnets behave, physicists can learn secrets about gravity and space.
